subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Apex Insure
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Hughes <sam.hughes@apexinsure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Apex Insure

Hi Sam — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Pain points you shared:
- Current latency spikes during claims-batch windows are causing downstream timeouts for the claims UI.
- Running models on shared cloud endpoints makes it hard to guarantee throughput for peak processing and to meet audit isolation requirements for certain PHI-containing pipelines.
- Cost unpredictability during heavy training/inference mix.

Current stack:
- On-prem GPU cluster for training (NVIDIA A100), production inference on a managed cloud endpoint today (multi-tenant).
- Core model: in-house fine-tuned transformer (sequence length ~1024) for claims classification + text normalization.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Predictable p95 latency <= 200ms at 1k token bursts for interactive claims lookup.
- Baseline sustained throughput ~100 TPS with headroom for 2x burst during peak batch windows.
- VPC isolation + KMS integration for keys, SOC 2 + audit trails for data access.
- Procurement timeline: PO within ~60 days if pricing and SLA align.

Recommended Redwood fit: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) to guarantee TPS and offer predictable unit economics. Key capability highlights we discussed:
- Reserve GPU pool with autoscale/burst policy (baseline pool to sustain 100 TPS, burst up to 2x with queued requests/fallback routing).
- Network isolation via Private deployment options (VPC peering) and KMS support for customer-managed keys.
- Observability: per-model token cost, latency P95 dashboards, and tracing to diagnose tail latency.

Open questions / assumptions:
1) Approx number of concurrent sessions and average request size (tokens) during peak windows? (you gave rough numbers but we'll confirm).
2) Any regulatory constraints that require fully air-gapped on-prem vs. VPC-only isolation?
3) Procurement/PO contact and budget code so we can prepare an SOW.

Next steps:
- Attached: dedicated-sizing-questionnaire.xlsx — please fill the sections marked 'required' before our tech deep-dive.
- I'll set up a technical deep-dive with Rafael (infra) and Marissa (solutions) next week to walk sizing and autoscale policies.
- I'll follow up with a draft SOW and an initial capacity/price estimate within 3 business days after the sizing doc.

Thanks — look forward to continuing.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0189
From: Sam Hughes <sam.hughes@apexinsure.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Apex Insure

Thanks Vanessa — solid summary, appreciate the clarity. A few clarifications from our side:

- Concurrent sessions: during peak claims hours we see ~80-120 concurrent sessions; batch jobs run overnight with spikes that effectively double request rate for ~30min windows.
- Average request size for the claims lookup flow is ~600 tokens; some longer normalization jobs hit ~1.5k tokens.
- For compliance: initially VPC/KMS isolation is acceptable; fully air-gapped on-prem would be a stretch goal for 2027.
- Procurement: looping in procurement@apexinsure.com for PO details — budget holds in Q2 if we can finalize scope and SLA.

I'll get the sizing questionnaire back by EOD Friday. One ask: can you call out the recommended burst policy (e.g., 2x baseline for 15-30 minutes) and any pricing implications? Procurement will want to see worst-case numbers.

Best,
Sam
Director, ML Platforms
Apex Insure
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Apex Insure — tech deep-dive request

Rafael / Marissa — forwarding the recap and Sam's notes. Key asks for the deep-dive:
- Validate recommended baseline capacity for 100 TPS at ~600 token avg and 2x burst up to 200 TPS for 15-30m.
- Call out GPU types (A100 vs H100) and estimated reserved pool sizes, plus autoscale policy options (max burst, cooldown).
- Prepare a short slide (1-2 pages) on isolation options and KMS integration steps for procurement.

Sam — Rafael will propose a sizing plan and we'll schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive next week. Pls confirm Tue/Wed availability.

— Vanessa
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Hughes <sam.hughes@apexinsure.com>
Date: 2026-03-30T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Apex Insure — tech deep-dive request

Thanks Vanessa — initial sizing notes based on the numbers Sam provided:

- Baseline: to sustain ~100 TPS at ~600 tokens/request (p95 latency target 200ms), we recommend reserving a pool equivalent to 8 A100-80GB GPUs (model/quantization dependent).
- Burst: allow autoscale up to 16 GPUs for short windows (15-30m). Use a two-tier policy: immediate soft-burst (queued requests, graceful degradation) up to +50% capacity, and hard-burst (spin additional reserved nodes) up to +100% with longer warm-up.
- Autoscale cooldown: 10m for soft-burst, 30-60m to scale down from hard-burst to avoid oscillation.
- Networking/security: VPC peering + private endpoints supported; KMS customer-key integration is straightforward — we provide audit logs and KMIP-compatible options.

Attachments I will bring to the deep-dive: a one-pager GPU sizing slide and a sample autoscale policy. I'll also enumerate cost delta between A100 vs H100 and quantized model profiles.

Proposed slots for deep-dive: Tue 3/31 10:00-10:45 PT or Wed 4/1 14:00-14:45 PT. Rafael and Marissa can attend either.

— Rafael
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
